notes: Switzerland Hardening I–III bindings. H1 four traveler/cash + H2 two resident/non-resident bindings preserved. Hardening III adds summary.business, rules.business_invoicing_settlement, and rules.banking_conversion_practicality only (total 9). CH-BIZ-07/08/11/12/13 unbound. country_overview and rules.exchange_controls remain for Hardening IV. No invoice/transfer/repatriation freedom; banking_conversion_practicality remains agnostic on general FX availability.

bindings.wording_boundary: May summarize, concisely: (1) unrestricted quantitative carriage of covered cash/instruments into/through/out of Switzerland under the FOCBS border-cash framework; (2) no spontaneous FOCBS declaration obligation for those covered instruments; (3) when questioned during a FOCBS check, truthful information is required; (4) a separate >= CHF 10,000 inquiry and FOCBS information-system registration layer; (5) below-threshold ML/TF suspicion may still trigger information powers; (6) provisional/temporary seizure on ML/TF suspicion remains possible and is not threshold-driven. Must NOT imply: Switzerland has no cash controls; nothing must be reported; CHF 10,000 declaration threshold; cash above CHF 10,000 is prohibited; CHF 10,000 carriage ceiling; permission required above CHF 10,000; unlimited and unregulated; no AML controls; below CHF 10,000 no controls; Meldung/Art. 6 as traveller declaration; FINMA capital-export monitoring; free import means no customs authority.

Inbound physical carriage framing: no quantitative inbound carriage ceiling for covered notes/coins/foreign currencies/bearer instruments under the reviewed FOCBS framework; no spontaneous FOCBS declaration obligation; inquiry/information-on-request and >= CHF 10,000 express-questioning package remain. Forbid: free import means no customs authority; no AML/TF control; >= CHF 10,000 requires permission; >= CHF 10,000 must be spontaneously declared; CHF 10,000 declaration threshold; CHF 10,000 carriage ceiling; statistical recording as the inbound rule; FINMA/SNB as inbound cash authorities; capital-account repatriation language in this border field.

Outbound physical carriage framing only (same architecture as inbound): unrestricted quantitative outbound carriage of covered instruments; no spontaneous FOCBS declaration; questioning/information and >= CHF 10,000 inquiry package remain. This field concerns physical border carriage, not capital-account repatriation. Forbid and treat as fidelity-invalid: earned from business or salary; Non-residents may freely repatriate; monitored under FINMA; Large capital exports by residents are monitored under FINMA; CHF 10,000 declaration threshold; CHF 10,000 carriage ceiling; permission required above CHF 10,000; spontaneous declaration at exit; free export means no customs controls.

Encode four architecture layers explicitly and keep them atomic: (A) no spontaneous FOCBS declaration threshold / no obligation to declare covered cash to FOCBS merely for crossing the border; (B) separate >= CHF 10,000 (mindestens / or more / equals or exceeds) inquiry package on express questioning (identity, origin/source, intended use, beneficial owner) plus FOCBS information-system registration at equals-or-exceeds CHF 10,000 — inquiry ≠ recording and neither is spontaneous declaration; (C) below-threshold ML/TF suspicion may still permit information powers under Art. 3 Abs. 2; (D) provisional/temporary seizure and Art. 5 lit. a–b refusal/false-information offence are suspicion/conduct mechanisms, not numeric carriage restrictions. Hard forbid: CHF 10,000 declaration threshold; declaration required at CHF 10,000; cash above CHF 10,000 must be declared; CHF 10,000 carriage ceiling; permission required above CHF 10,000; below CHF 10,000 no controls; no declaration for normal amounts; large amounts recorded for statistical and AML purposes (unsupported statistical purpose); large or suspicious cash movements subject to AML reporting by financial institutions as the border rule; Meldung/Art. 6 as traveller declaration; automatic confiscation; permanent seizure as the threshold consequence.

Describe only governed H2 AML/account-relationship compliance conditions where a relevant financial intermediary establishes or maintains a client relationship with a resident: contracting-party identity verification (AMLA / bank CDB account-opening where applicable); beneficial-owner identification/verification and bank BO statement mechanics; repeated verification on doubt; risk-based periodic record updating; conditional enhanced clarification (unusual / higher-risk / crime-TF indicators); institutional money-laundering risk tolerance that may place certain clients/countries/services outside acceptance limits; and, for high-risk relationships, detailed source-of-assets clarification and careful monitoring of higher-risk transactions. H2 did NOT establish a statutory resident right to open or hold bank or foreign-currency accounts — do not state or imply such entitlement. Hard forbid: Swiss residents may hold and maintain foreign currency accounts freely; residents have a right to foreign-currency accounts; residents may open accounts without restriction; freely; KYC proves entitlement; successful KYC guarantees acceptance; without prior approval; no approval is required; unrestricted cross-border transfers; unrestricted repatriation; authorised banks and financial institutions as a vague entitlement actor class without AML scope. Residence-specific entitlement or exemption is not established by these H2 claims; do not assert residents and non-residents are treated identically under all Swiss law.

Describe governed AML/account-relationship requirements where a relevant financial intermediary establishes a client relationship — without asserting universal non-resident account entitlement or the opposite ban. May include identity verification, beneficial-owner requirements, bank CDB account-opening mechanics where applicable, risk-based updates, conditional enhanced DD, institutional risk tolerance / outside-tolerance acceptance, and high-risk conditional source-of-assets monitoring. Governed agnosticism on universal entitlement. Hard forbid: Non-residents may open and operate foreign currency accounts; transfer funds freely; without prior approval; freely; all non-residents are entitled to Swiss accounts; foreign clients are legally guaranteed access; all non-residents are high risk; all non-residents require enhanced DD; foreign residence automatically requires source-of-wealth proof; unrestricted transfer/repatriation rights; non-residents have no right to accounts (unsupported opposite). Country risk ≠ residency class. Institutional refusal under risk tolerance ≠ statutory nationality/residence prohibition.

Mechanism-based business summary only within bound H3 claims: Swiss private law (CO Art. 84) contemplates foreign-currency pecuniary debts; local-currency substitution at maturity is possible subject to the actual-currency contractual exception; Swiss VAT rules separately recognise foreign-currency invoices/receipts for tax classification and require CHF conversion for VAT assessment using FTA monthly average or daily sell rates; SIC provides central Swiss payment infrastructure and domestic account-to-account instant payments operate within their evidenced scope. Hard forbid: full freedom; freely; businesses enjoy full freedom to hold, transfer, convert and repatriate; Business transactions may be invoiced and settled in foreign currency or CHF (as a universal legal rule); Cross-border payments and repatriation of funds are handled freely; unrestricted settlement; unrestricted cross-border payments; unrestricted repatriation; no approval required; fully liberalised; no exchange controls; widely available FX conversion; SIC proves international transfer freedom; domestic instant payment equals international/cross-currency instant payment; VAT conversion equals CHF-only settlement; accounting currency equals payment currency; authorised banks and financial institutions as a vague entitlement class. Do not bind or import narrow Ukraine sanctions or future ISA into this summary.

Distinguish explicitly: invoice ≠ debt denomination ≠ VAT classification ≠ payment currency ≠ accounting currency ≠ settlement rail. May describe Art. 84 FCY-denominated monetary obligations and local-currency substitution / actual-currency exception; VAT Art. 45 foreign-currency invoice/receipt classification and CHF conversion for VAT assessment with FTA rate mechanics; SIC and domestic instant-payment infrastructure within evidenced scope. Must NOT state: Business transactions may be invoiced and settled in foreign currency or CHF as a universal legal rule; Cross-border payments and repatriation are handled freely; full freedom; freely; unrestricted transfers; no approval required; authorised banks and financial institutions as legacy entitlement wording; VAT conversion requires commercial settlement in CHF; accounting/reporting currency equals invoice or payment currency. Do not bind CH-BIZ-07/08/11/12/13.

Evidence-grounded infrastructure only: SIC is central Swiss payment infrastructure within its evidenced participant/large-value/retail scope; domestic account-to-account instant payments operate within the evidenced domestic scope. This field remains agnostic on general customer FX-conversion availability — H3 did not establish it. Hard forbid: Foreign exchange conversion and transfers are widely available; easy conversion; unrestricted conversion; competitive rates; low friction; licensed money exchange houses throughout Switzerland; ATMs provide general FX conversion; all banks provide conversion; cross-border payments are free/unrestricted; SIC performs general customer FX conversion; domestic instant payments are cross-currency; no approval required; freely; full freedom. Do not force Art. 84 / VAT / FTA tax-conversion claims into this banking field.
